## Libraries

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(forcats)
library(lme4)
library(corrplot)
library(clipr)
library(igraph)
library(ggraph)
```

## Import data

import data

```{r}
raw_df <- read.csv("../data/responses_combined.csv")
raw_df <- raw_df %>% 
  group_by(subject_id) %>%
  mutate(ai_score = sum(cognitive_1, cognitive_2, 
                         affective_1, affective_2, 
                         behavioral_1, behavioral_2)/6)

# remove subject_id = "" (test trials)
raw_df <- raw_df %>%
  filter(subject_id != "")
```

```{r}
head(raw_df)
```

```{r}
categories <- lapply(categories, tolower)

assign_category <- function(response) {
  if (is.na(response) || response == "") return(NA_character_)
  for (cat_name in names(categories)) {
    if (response %in% categories[[cat_name]]) {
      return(cat_name)
    }
  }
  return("other")
}

analysis_df <- raw_df %>%
  mutate(across(
    .cols = c(word_1, word_2, word_3, word_4, word_5),
    .fns  = ~ sapply(tolower(trimws(.x)), assign_category),
    .names = "category_{.col}"
  )) %>%
  rename_with(~ gsub("category_word_", "category_", .x), starts_with("category_word_"))

# add broad characterizations
social_cats   <- c(
  "gender", "sexuality", "other_sgi", "persona", "region", "locale",
  "education", "profession", "race_ethnicity", "social_standing", "other_soc"
)
phys_cats   <- c(
  "age", "appearance", "attractiveness", "health", "other_phys"
)
psych_cats   <- c(
  "agreeableness", "extraversion", "openness", "emo_stab", "cons", "other_psych"
)
speech_cats   <- c(
  "contour", "voice_qual", "intensity", "speech_rhythm", "other_speech"
)


analysis_df <- analysis_df %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    n_social   = sum(c_across(category_1:category_5) %in% social_cats),
    n_phys   = sum(c_across(category_1:category_5) %in% phys_cats),
    n_psych   = sum(c_across(category_1:category_5) %in% psych_cats),
    n_speech = sum(c_across(category_1:category_5) %in% speech_cats),
    n_content  = sum(c_across(category_1:category_5) == "content"),
    any_artificial = any(c_across(word_1:word_5) %in% 
                           c("AI", "Ai", "ai", "Ai generated", "Artificial",
                             "artificial", "automatic", "Computer",
                             "digital", "Fake", "fake", "fake?", "inauthentic",
                             "inhuman", "manufactured", "robot",
                             "Robotic", "robotic", "Technological", "unnatural",
                             "Unrealistic", "unrealistic", "untenable" ,"off")
                         )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

## Data Analysis - Across Speakers

```{r}
ggplot(analysis_df, aes(x = ai_score, 
                        y = humanness_rating)) +
  geom_point(color = "black", 
             size = 3,
             alpha = 0.75) +       
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red") +
  theme_minimal() 

cor(analysis_df$ai_score, analysis_df$humanness_rating, method = "pearson")
```

Humanness rating is minimally correlated with AI attitude score (Pearson's r = 0.1614323).

## Data Analysis - By Speaker

```{r}
analysis_df %>% 
  group_by(voice) %>% 
  summarise(
    mean = mean(humanness_rating),
    sd = sd(humanness_rating), 
    median = median(humanness_rating)
  )
```

visualizations

```{r}
ggplot(analysis_df, aes(
  x = voice, 
  y = humanness_rating, 
  fill = voice)) + 
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.4, size = 1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo") + 
  coord_flip() + 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r}
ggplot(analysis_df, aes(
  x = reorder(voice, humanness_rating, FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE), 
  y = humanness_rating, 
  fill = reorder(voice, humanness_rating, FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE))) + 
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.4, size = 1) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean, 
    geom = "point", 
    shape = 21, 
    size = 1, 
    fill = "white", 
    color = "black"
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo") + 
  labs(x = "Voice", y = "Humanness Rating") +
  coord_flip() + 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    aspect.ratio = 1
  )
```

```{r}
long_df %>% 
  filter(cat != "content") %>% 
```
```{r}
  mutate(higher_order_cat = case_when(
    cat %in% social_cats ~ "Social",
    cat %in% phys_cats ~ "Physical",
    cat %in% psych_cats ~ "Psychological",
    cat %in% speech_cats ~ "Speech",
    TRUE ~ "Other" 
  )) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(y = voice, fill = higher_order_cat), position = "fill") +
  labs(
    x = "Proportion of Non-Content Responses",
    y = "Voice",
    fill = "Category Type"
  ) + 
  theme(
    legend.text = element_text(size = 6), 
    legend.key.size = unit(0.3, "cm"),       
    legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)    
  )
```

reorder the bars of the plot above to make it increasing order of "social" category:

```{r}
cat_colors <- c(
  "Social"        = "#77AADD", # Deep indigo
  "Psychological" = "#FFAABB", # Muted rose
  "Physical"      = "#44BB99", # Seafoam teal
  "Speech"        = "#EE8866", # Warm sand
  "Other"         = "#EEDD88"  # Pale gray
)


long_df %>% 
  filter(cat != "content") %>% 
  mutate(
    higher_order_cat = case_when(
      cat %in% social_cats ~ "Social",
      cat %in% phys_cats ~ "Physical",
      cat %in% psych_cats ~ "Psychological",
      cat %in% speech_cats ~ "Speech",
      TRUE ~ "Other" 
    ),
    # Set exact left-to-right order (edit the sequence inside c() as desired)
    higher_order_cat = factor(
      higher_order_cat, 
      levels = c("Social", "Psychological", "Physical", "Speech", "Other")
    ),
    # Order bars by increasing proportion of "Social"
    voice = fct_reorder(voice, higher_order_cat == "Social", .fun = mean)
  ) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(
    aes(y = voice, fill = higher_order_cat), 
    position = position_fill(reverse = TRUE)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cat_colors) +
  labs(
    x = "Proportion of Non-Content Responses",
    y = "Voice",
    fill = "Category Type"
  ) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.text = element_text(size = 6), 
    legend.key.size = unit(0.3, "cm"),       
    legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)    
  )

```

## Sankey prep

```{r}
category_counts <- analysis_df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = category_1:category_5,
    names_to = "word_number",
    values_to = "category"
  ) %>%
  count(category, sort = TRUE)
```

```{r}
View(category_counts)
```

## Question: Person-like attributions persist, even at low humanness?

```{r}
long_df <- analysis_df %>%
  pivot_longer(category_1:category_5, names_to="slot", values_to="cat") %>%
  filter(cat != "content") %>%
  mutate(is_human = cat %in% c(social_cats, phys_cats, psych_cats),
         slot_num = as.integer(gsub("category_","",slot)))

subj_df <- long_df %>% # subject-clustering accounts for between-subj design
  group_by(subject_id, voice, humanness_rating) %>%
  summarise(n_human = sum(is_human), n_total = n(), .groups="drop")

# models for pilot data 
## simple model, no random effect of subject (bc of a single trial structure)
m_social_1 <- glm(cbind(n_human, n_total - n_human) ~ scale(humanness_rating), 
                  data = subj_df, 
                  family = quasibinomial)
summary(m_social_1)
## added voice fixed effect
m_social_2 <- glm(cbind(n_human, n_total - n_human) ~ scale(humanness_rating) + 
                  voice, 
                  data = subj_df, 
                  family = quasibinomial)
summary(m_social_2)

# which model better accounts for variance? 
anova(m_social_1, m_social_2, test = "F")
```

Model results suggest that perceived humanness modulates the attribution of social descriptors, such that higher "humanness" ratings positively predict a greater rate of social descriptors ($β = 0.34722, p < .001$).

Adding voice as a fixed effect did not attenuate the humanness slope ($β = 0.34722, p < .001$ in simple model vs. $β = 0.371049, p < .001$ in complex model). Model comparison (using an F-test to account for overdispersion in the quasibinomial model) revealed no significant main effect of voice, $F(17, 483) = 1.4665, p = .102$.

Note: Because the design was between subjects, I modeled social/phys/psych attribution at the participant level rather than the descriptor level. For each participant, I computed the number of non-content descriptors that could be described as social, physical, or psychological out of the total non-content descriptors produced, and then I fit a quasibinomial GLM predicting this proportion from z-scored humanness rating.

```{r}
# predicted probabilities
newdat <- data.frame(humanness_rating = c(0, 30, 50, 66.6, 100))
newdat$z <- (newdat$humanness_rating - mean(analysis_df$humanness_rating)) / 
  sd(analysis_df$humanness_rating)
pred <- predict(m_social_1, newdata = data.frame(humanness_rating = newdat$humanness_rating),
                type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)
newdat$p     <- plogis(pred$fit)
newdat$lo    <- plogis(pred$fit - 1.96 * pred$se.fit)
newdat$hi    <- plogis(pred$fit + 1.96 * pred$se.fit)
newdat

newdat <- data.frame(humanness_rating = seq(0, 100, by = 2))
pred <- predict(m_social_1, newdata = data.frame(humanness_rating = newdat$humanness_rating,
                                             voice = "gracie_valley"),  # arbitrary ref level
                type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)
newdat$p  <- plogis(pred$fit)
newdat$lo <- plogis(pred$fit - 1.96 * pred$se.fit)
newdat$hi <- plogis(pred$fit + 1.96 * pred$se.fit)

# visualization
ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = newdat, aes(humanness_rating, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), 
              alpha = 0.2, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(data = newdat, aes(humanness_rating, p), color = "steelblue", size = 1) +
  geom_jitter(data = subj_df, 
              aes(humanness_rating, n_human / n_total),
              width = 0.5, height = 0.02, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey") +
  labs(x = "Humanness Rating", 
       y = "P(social or psychological | non-content descriptor)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Social/psych/phys attribution rate remained substantial across the humanness range, even for voices rated near the bottom of the scale, roughly 60–73% of non-content descriptors were social/psych/phys, well above a floor of zero.

## Question: Transition Probabilities?

```{r}
transitions <- analysis_df %>%
  select(subject_id, voice, category_1:category_5) %>%
  pivot_longer(category_1:category_5, names_to="slot", values_to="cat") %>%
  mutate(slot = as.integer(gsub("category_","",slot))) %>%
  filter(cat != "content") %>%
  arrange(subject_id, slot) %>%
  group_by(subject_id) %>%
  mutate(next_cat = lead(cat)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(next_cat)) %>%
  ungroup()

# raw transition probability matrix
trans_mat <- transitions %>%
  count(cat, next_cat) %>%
  group_by(cat) %>%
  mutate(p = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup()

# add marginal probabilities 
marginals <- transitions %>%
  count(next_cat) %>%
  mutate(p_marginal = n / sum(n)) %>%
  select(next_cat, p_marginal)

# matrix with marginals 
trans_mat_w_margin <- trans_mat %>%
  left_join(marginals, by = "next_cat") %>%
  mutate(lift = p / p_marginal)

# plot priming relationships
trans_mat_w_margin %>%
mutate(log2_lift = log2(lift)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = next_cat, y = cat, fill = log2_lift)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Semantic Priming (Red = Positive Priming, Blue = Suppression)")
```

This can be challenging to interpret, given that there are many single-instance category sequences (e.g., age-age and emo_stab-profession only occur once). High lift can be interpreted as increased likelihood of the second (next) category occurring after the first category, compared to the overall probability of the second category in the dataset. Low lift is a decreased likelihood of the second category occurring after the first category, compared to the overall probability of the second category in the dataset.

We see some within-category facilitation (e.g., an appearance mention increases the likelihood of another appearance mention). Inhibitory relationships seem weaker, and I can't really identify any consistent patterning.

```{r}
# keep only transitions that happened at least 10 times
robust_priming <- trans_mat_w_margin %>%
  filter(n >= 10) %>%
  arrange(desc(lift))

# plot robust (frequent) priming relationships
robust_priming %>%
  mutate(log2_lift = log2(lift)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = next_cat, y = cat, fill = log2_lift)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Semantic Priming (Red = Positive Priming, Blue = Suppression)")
```

Frequent positive priming between: naturalness-naturalness, profession-profession, gender-age. Frequent but weak inhibition between: education-emo_stab, education-gender, gender-education, agreeablness-voice_qual, voice_qual-agreeableness

```{r}
# adjust lift/count threshold as needed
graph_df <- trans_mat_w_margin %>% 
  filter(n >= 5, lift > 1) 

g <- graph_from_data_frame(graph_df, directed = TRUE)

# calculate node importance (degree) to control text size
V(g)$node_size <- degree(g, mode = "all")

ggraph(g, layout = "fr") + 
  geom_edge_loop(
    aes(alpha = lift), 
    color = "gray70", 
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(1, 'mm'), type = "closed")
  ) +
  geom_edge_link(
    aes(alpha = lift), 
    color = "gray70", 
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(1, 'mm'), type = "closed"),
    end_cap = circle(4, 'mm') 
  ) +
  geom_node_point(
    size = 1, 
    color = "black") + 
  geom_node_text(
    aes(label = name, size = node_size), 
    color = "black", 
    fontface = "bold",
    repel = TRUE # helps prevent text overlap
  ) +
  scale_size(range = c(2, 4), guide = "none") + 
  scale_edge_alpha(range = c(0.4, 1), guide = "none") +
  theme_void()
```

The attempt at a network visualization is still hard to read, but gender, education, and extraversion are more likely following many different types of categories... naturalness feeds into more naturalness comments, and profesions, persona, and region also seem to iterate on themselves.

## \[VAD v1\] Question: Is AI attitude a predictor of lexicon affect?

using: **The NRC Valence, Arousal, and Dominance Lexicon**

<https://emilhvitfeldt.github.io/textdata/reference/lexicon_nrc_vad.html>

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(textdata)
library(broom)
```

```{r}
###prep

word_cols <- paste0("word_", 1:5)

required_cols <- c(
  "ai_score",
  "humanness_rating",
  word_cols
)

# Clean words for matching:
# - convert to lowercase
# - remove leading/trailing spaces
# - remove punctuation at the beginning/end

clean_word <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  x <- str_to_lower(str_trim(x))
  x <- str_remove(x, "^\\p{P}+")
  x <- str_remove(x, "\\p{P}+$")
  x <- str_remove(x, "`")
  str_trim(x)
}

#content words storage
content_words <- categories[[1]] %>%
  unlist(use.names = FALSE) %>%
  clean_word() %>%
  unique()
```

```{r}

#Filter participants based on humanness_rating (i.e., if they do not believe this is AI voice more than 50%, remove from this analysis?-- we can totally lower this value...)

participants_filtered <- analysis_df %>%
  mutate(
    participant_row = paste0("P", row_number()),
    ai_score = as.numeric(as.character(ai_score)),
    humanness_rating = as.numeric(as.character(humanness_rating))
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(humanness_rating),
    humanness_rating >= 50
  )

#------check how many participants remain-------#
cat(
  "Number of participants before filtering:",
  nrow(analysis_df), "\n"
)

cat(
  "Number of participants after filtering:",
  nrow(participants_filtered), "\n"
)
```

```{r}

#Convert resps into long format

responses_long <- participants_filtered %>%
  select(
    participant_row,
    ai_score,
    humanness_rating,
    all_of(word_cols)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(word_cols),
    names_to = "word_position",
    values_to = "original_word"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    word_clean = clean_word(original_word),

    is_nonempty = !is.na(word_clean) & word_clean != "",

    is_content_word = is_nonempty &
      word_clean %in% content_words
  )
```

```{r}

#Count content words and usable responses

word_counts <- responses_long %>%
  group_by(participant_row) %>%
  summarise(
    n_words_entered = sum(is_nonempty),

    n_content_words_removed = sum(is_content_word),

    n_noncontent_words = sum(
      is_nonempty & !is_content_word
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

```

```{r}
vad_raw <- textdata::lexicon_nrc_vad()

vad_lexicon <- vad_raw %>%
  mutate(
    word = clean_word(.data$Word)
  ) %>%
  select(
    word,
    Valence,

```

```{r}
#match participant responses with the VAD Lexicon

vad_word_level <- responses_long %>%
  # Remove empty responses and content words
  filter(
    is_nonempty,
    !is_content_word
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    vad_lexicon,
    by = c("word_clean" = "word")

# Inspect the matched words
print(
  vad_word_level %>%
```

```{r}
unmatched_words <- vad_word_level %>%
  filter(is.na(Valence)) %>%
  count(word_clean, sort = TRUE)

cat("\nWords not found in the NRC VAD Lexicon:\n")
print(unmatched_words)

```

```{r}
#  Calculate each participant's mean VAD scores

# Helper function: return NA rather than NaN
# when a participant has no matched words

mean_or_na <- function(x) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) {
    NA_real_
  } else {
    mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
}

vad_summary <- vad_word_level %>%
  group_by(participant_row) %>%
  summarise(
    n_vad_words = sum(!is.na(Valence)),

    n_vad_unmatched = sum(is.na(Valence)),

    mean_valence = mean_or_na(Valence),

    mean_arousal = mean_or_na(Arousal),

    mean_dominance = mean_or_na(Dominance),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Combine word counts and VAD scores.
# Keep participants who have zero matched words as well.

participant_vad <- participants_filtered %>%
  select(
    participant_row,
    ai_score,
    humanness_rating
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    word_counts,
    by = "participant_row"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    vad_summary,
    by = "participant_row"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        n_words_entered,
        n_content_words_removed,
        n_noncontent_words,
        n_vad_words,
        n_vad_unmatched
      ),
      ~ replace_na(.x, 0L)
    ),

    # Proportion of non-content words successfully matched
    vad_coverage = if_else(
      n_noncontent_words > 0,
      n_vad_words / n_noncontent_words,
      NA_real_
    )
  )

# Inspect participant-level data
head(participant_vad)
```

```{r}

#  Linear regression:
#     Does AI attitude predict lexical affect?

fit_vad_model <- function(outcome, data) {

  # Only include participants with both an AI score
  # and a valid VAD score

  model_data <- data %>%
    filter(
      is.finite(ai_score),
      is.finite(.data[[outcome]])
    )

  # Check whether there is enough variation to fit a model
  if (
    nrow(model_data) < 3 ||
    n_distinct(model_data$ai_score) < 2 ||
    n_distinct(model_data[[outcome]]) < 2
  ) {
    return(
      tibble(
        dimension = outcome,
        n = nrow(model_data),
        estimate = NA_real_,
        std.error = NA_real_,
        statistic = NA_real_,
        p.value = NA_real_,
        conf.low = NA_real_,
        conf.high = NA_real_,
        r_squared = NA_real_
      )
    )
  }

  # Fit linear model
  fit <- lm(
    reformulate("ai_score", response = outcome),
    data = model_data
  )

  model_stats <- broom::glance(fit)

  # Extract the AI attitude coefficient
  broom::tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term == "ai_score") %>%
    transmute(
      dimension = outcome,
      n = nobs(fit),
      estimate,
      std.error,
      statistic,
      p.value,
      conf.low,
      conf.high,
      r_squared = model_stats$r.squared
    )
}

# Run three separate models
vad_model_results <- purrr::map_dfr(
  c(
    "mean_valence",
    "mean_arousal",
    "mean_dominance"
  ),
  fit_vad_model,
  data = participant_vad
) %>%
  mutate(
    # Correct for testing three affect dimensions
    p_adj_BH = p.adjust(
      p.value,
      method = "BH"
    )
  )

tibble(vad_model_results)



```

```{r}
# Helper function: return NA rather than NaN
# when a participant has no matched words

mean_or_na <- function(x) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) {
    NA_real_
  } else {
    mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
}

vad_summary <- vad_word_level %>%
  group_by(participant_row) %>%
```
